items.prompt: Do zero sums Σe_i and Σx_i e_i establish independent model errors?

options.text: No; these are fitted-training algebraic constraints
options.why: The identities can hold for a badly misspecified curved response.

options.text: Yes; any two zero sums prove independence
options.why: Two scalar identities do not specify a joint distribution.

options.text: Yes; normality follows from the fitting algorithm
options.why: Least squares does not manufacture normal errors.

options.text: Yes, if the residuals also have zero average
options.why: The fitted intercept already imposes that average; repeating a fit identity adds no independence evidence.

items.explanation: Residual checks must go beyond identities imposed by the fitting procedure.
